prompt:
Write 11 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim, in time order. Injury: knee injury. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1171; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment ran somewhat longer than usual for this injury.
- Years ago the patient had a small strain in the same area that healed fully.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim received today for a left-turn collision at an intersection involving the insured's vehicle and a second vehicle. The claimant reports a knee injury from the impact and is not represented by an attorney.

Entry 2: Confirmed the driver is listed on the policy and that the policy was in force at the time of the loss. Coverage appears in order for this claim.

Entry 3: Spoke with the claimant, who described the crash as a left turn that was struck on the driver's side by oncoming traffic. The account was clear and consistent with the initial report.

Entry 4: Police report reviewed. Officers confirm the claimant was seated in the vehicle when they arrived on scene.

Entry 5: Obtained photos from the scene and statements from two independent witnesses. Both describe the collision in the same way the claimant did, and the other driver's account matches as well.

Entry 6: Reviewed vehicle damage with the appraiser. The damage is largely consistent with the impact described, and no prior damage to the vehicle is known from our records or the claimant's history.

Entry 7: Checked the vehicle's claim and inspection history. Nothing points to damage that existed before the coverage start date.

Entry 8: Medical records received for the knee injury. The type of injury and the force involved in the crash line up well with one another.

Entry 9: Claimant's treatment has continued for somewhat longer than is typical for this kind of knee injury. Requested the treating provider's notes to understand the course of care.

Entry 10: Prior records show a minor strain in the same knee area several years ago. That episode resolved fully with treatment and has no bearing on the current injury based on the medical review so far.

Entry 11: Every conversation with the claimant has produced the same account of events and injuries. Claim remains open pending the final medical review and a settlement evaluation.
